name: Magna Carta, Foundation of English Constitutional Law
summary: Barons force King John to seal Magna Carta at Runnymede, 63 clauses limiting royal prerogative. Key provisions: no free man imprisoned except by judgment of peers or law of the land (habeas corpus precedent); no taxation without consent of the Great Council; and a committee of 25 barons to enforce compliance. John immediately requests papal annulment (granted); the First Barons' War follows. But reissued versions of Magna Carta (1216, 1217, 1225) establish it as permanent constitutional law.

_quarry.structural_significance: Magna Carta is the foundational document of English constitutionalism; its principle that the king is under the law (not above it) shapes English political development from the 13th century through the Glorious Revolution (1688); Clause 39's protection against arbitrary imprisonment becomes the philosophical basis for habeas corpus, due process, and the rule of law in the Anglo-American legal tradition; its modern importance far exceeds its original medieval significance
